evidence: Codex 0.155.1 upstream writes provider-owned state under CODEX_HOME/.tmp, including plugin-share-local-paths-v1.json and rollout-maintenance.lock. v0.4.2 admits .tmp only through the initialized-capability provider roots after CLROOM's v2 state marker exists; both a fresh uninitialized shadow and the legacy .sandbox_migration compatibility path remain unable to authorize preexisting .tmp, and unknown top-level siblings still fail closed.

Regression coverage proves initialized .tmp provider state survives a later CLROOM launch, preexisting unowned .tmp still fails closed, real Codex qualification executes twice against one synthetic home, pre-tag whole-plugin evidence cannot be written until a post-interactive clean relaunch succeeds, and canonical readiness owns the exact-tag Draft verifier.
Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock advance only the package version to 0.4.2; no runtime or build dependency is added, removed, or replaced.

Real Codex provider qualification requires two provider observations on the same synthetic HOME and v2 evidence. The provider-canary contract itself now asserts the lifecycle-v2 smoke, two-run qualifier, tag-evidence fields and v0.4.2 negative fixture so release hardening cannot silently regress to the former v1 contract.

Public discovery verification now validates the explicit sitemap source contract in CI and, after same-SHA CI plus Pages deployment, probes the canonical published sitemap over HTTPS with redirects refused, bounded retries/size, XML parsing, canonical-host/path enforcement, duplicate rejection, and canonical-home presence before IndexNow notification.

The pre-tag helper accepts only lifecycle-aware Codex v2 evidence with a successful clean relaunch after the interactive selected-plugin TUI. A new canonical verify-draft-release.sh reconciles exact tag/SHA identity, Draft assets, checksums, attestations, current provider pins, local pre-tag/Draft evidence, and every exact-tag push Action before any publish gate; canonical readiness verifies this verifier is executable and shell-valid.

Current README and Codex/Claude/limitations documentation identify v0.4.2 as the candidate capability version, while CHANGELOG records that v0.4.1 remained an unpublished Draft candidate and that v0.4.2 supersedes it.

The published GitHub Pages sitemap is now checked end to end against the canonical y-sor.github.io/clean-room-launcher URL surface, so malformed XML, foreign-host entries, duplicates, missing canonical home, redirects, and non-XML responses fail the discovery pipeline instead of being inferred from source configuration alone.

near_misses.durable_control: Codex activation requires both exact-bundle projection into the active private shadow PluginStore and session-layer exact plugin enablement; session flags alone are not treated as qualification evidence.

Shadow PluginStore selection is single-bundle only, verified by path+digest ownership marker and cache-only-selected checks; stale owned projections are reconciled, while unknown siblings or tampered projections fail closed and are preserved rather than blindly deleted.

Projection preserves executable bits while removing write bits recursively; provider sandbox also write-denies the shadow plugin cache and marker, with regression tests for read-only and executable semantics.
Provider identity/version, installed source identity/digest and projected bundle are revalidated after planning and again immediately before provider exec; any drift refuses before provider birth.
When CLROOM plugin selection is active, raw Codex config/profile/feature/plugin controls are refused before provider birth; arguments after the provider terminator remain literal.

Canonical provider-pins.sh records exact current-stable versions and npm integrity; check-provider-pins.sh verifies latest tags and integrity during candidate provisioning and again at the action-time tag boundary.

Release contract tests and qualification evidence verification consume the canonical pinned provider versions instead of duplicating stale provider version/digest literals; evidence is rejected unless its provider version exactly matches the pinned canary version.
Public identity tests include features.remote_plugin=false in the exact Codex clean argv contract while preserving native Codex process identity and passthrough semantics.
The post-v0.4.0 release delta explicitly verifies the exported SBOM attestation bundle with the CycloneDX predicate before publication.

Protected-tag helper refreshes main/tag/ruleset/release-contract/provider-pin state at action time, compares local provider version and bytes to pretag evidence, performs one tag push, then reconciles the authoritative remote result.

Release readiness provisions the pinned current Codex canary before full locked tests; negative qualification tests derive the executable's actual provider version and therefore exercise the fail-closed harness instead of returning early or failing before evidence creation.

Codex v0.4.1 uses a new .clroom-clean-state-v2/.clroom-state-v2 shadow generation. Legacy v1 shadow state is preserved but never imported or deleted; regression coverage seeds stale plugin-cache content in v1 and proves selected projection starts in clean v2 state while the existing unknown-sibling guard remains fail-closed.

Codex state management and sandbox write denial consume the same shared active shadow-generation constant; regression coverage requires the sandbox profile to protect the active v2 plugin cache and not the preserved legacy v1 cache.

near_misses.failure_mode: Codex CLI dotted-path encoding can misaddress provider-owned plugin IDs, and selected whole-plugin MCP capability can remain disabled by provider MCP policy.
near_misses.durable_control: Atomic root-level exact-plugin config with MCP enablement derived only from the captured exact bundle inventory, covered by real-provider clean→selected→clean qualification.

near_misses.failure_mode: Pinned Codex 0.155.1 legitimately creates CODEX_HOME/.tmp state after CLROOM shadow initialization; the previous static allowlist rejected that state on the next launch.
near_misses.durable_control: The initialized v2 shadow admits the exact provider-owned .tmp top-level class, with regression fixtures for pinned upstream plugin-share and rollout-maintenance state plus a negative test proving preexisting unowned .tmp remains fail-closed.

near_misses.failure_mode: The v0.4.1 pre-tag smoke proved clean→selected→clean before the selected interactive TUI, then accepted evidence without proving the next clean launch after provider-written interactive state.
near_misses.durable_control: Codex pre-tag evidence schema v2 requires clean→selected→clean→selected interactive TUI→clean on the same persistent shadow; push-release-tag.sh rejects evidence without post_interactive_clean_confirmed=true.

near_misses.failure_mode: A successful Release workflow was initially treated as the relevant Draft signal while a separate exact-tag CI run had failed, so manual review could miss an independent tag-triggered blocker.
near_misses.durable_control: Canonical verify-draft-release.sh requires all exact-tag push Actions for the exact source SHA, including CI and Release, to be completed successfully and also reconciles Draft identity/assets/attestations/provider pins/local evidence before a publish verdict.

near_misses.failure_mode: The previous evidence field name persistent_provider_state_unchanged overstated what the smoke actually fingerprinted: ambient config.toml and the ambient plugin tree, while CLROOM shadow provider state is intentionally allowed to evolve.
near_misses.durable_control: Codex v2 evidence names the measured invariant ambient_config_and_plugin_tree_unchanged and separately proves provider_state_lifecycle_closed, preventing evidence semantics from claiming stronger state immutability than was measured.

near_misses.failure_mode: Source-level sitemap configuration could pass while the deployed GitHub Pages sitemap was malformed, redirected, stale, foreign-hosted, or otherwise unusable by crawlers.
near_misses.durable_control: CI validates the sitemap template and negative fixtures, while the same-SHA post-Pages IndexNow workflow fetches the canonical live sitemap with redirects refused and bounded XML/canonical-URL validation before search-engine notification.

artifact_capability_gates.requirement: Build exact accepted-main v0.4.2 archive on macOS Apple Silicon with pinned current-stable Codex 0.155.1 and an already-installed exact Codex plugin; prove clean→selected→clean MCP visibility, normal selected-plugin interactive TUI without a model prompt, then a final clean relaunch on the same persistent CLROOM shadow after provider-written state; bind v2 evidence to exact provider/plugin bytes and unchanged ambient config/plugin inputs.

Download exact Draft Release v0.4.2 archive, verify checksums/provenance/CycloneDX bundles, prove clean→selected→clean Codex plugin behavior against the Draft bytes, and pass canonical exact-tag pre-publish reconciliation including all tag-triggered Actions and accepted local evidence.

Requalify the shipped Claude whole-plugin path on pinned current-stable Claude Code 2.1.278 using exact accepted-main v0.4.2 bytes; prove clean absence, selected presence, no newly admitted sibling, no plugin errors, unchanged persistent provider config, and normal selected-plugin interactive TUI without a model prompt.

Re-run the Claude plugin capability smoke on exact Draft Release v0.4.2 bytes after checksum and attestation verification, bound to Claude Code 2.1.278, then include its evidence in canonical exact-tag pre-publish reconciliation.

product_outcome: Ship v0.4.2 as the bounded exact Codex whole-plugin selective-restore slice from the published v0.4.0 baseline, while repairing provider-written state lifecycle compatibility and promoting fail-closed pre-tag and pre-publish reconciliation so a successful first launch or one successful workflow cannot be mistaken for release readiness. The same candidate also hardens public discovery by verifying the deployed canonical sitemap before IndexNow notification.

contract_evolution_review.rationale: The unpublished v0.4.1 Draft exposed two missing lifecycle boundaries and one review-reconciliation gap: legitimate pinned-provider state could make the next launch fail, interactive pre-tag state was not followed by a clean relaunch, and a reviewer could inspect the Release workflow while missing a separate failed exact-tag CI run. Because these are release near-misses, v0.4.2 promotes durable runtime, evidence, tag-gate, CI lifecycle, and exact-tag pre-publish reconciliation controls rather than deleting state or relying on manual vigilance. The candidate also closes a public-discovery verification gap by promoting the sitemap from source-only checks to a same-SHA deployed canary before IndexNow notification.
